The one previous-generation choice is the router: the Navigation API became Baseline Newly available in Jan 2026 and is the current platform routing primitive for this Chromium-only app, while the History API used here is still supported, not deprecated.

churn_resistance.rationale: The data layer and configuration are genuinely well isolated and a Vite upgrade would touch almost nothing, but the render layer is hand-managed: no types at the API boundary, stale-render cancellation enforced at 13 scattered sites, outerHTML re-renders with recursive listener attachment, and HTML safety dependent on every call site remembering to escape.

findings.issue: Router built on History API with manual anchor-click interception plus pushState/popstate/hashchange glue; it misses non-click navigations (form submits, location changes) and re-implements ~50 lines the platform now provides.
findings.suggestion: Use the Navigation API (Baseline Newly available Jan 2026, in Chrome since 102): navigation.addEventListener('navigate', e => e.intercept(() => renderRoute(e.destination))) replaces the click/popstate/hashchange handlers.

findings.issue: Route changes guarded by a manual renderToken checked after each of ~13 awaits; in-flight requests keep running after navigation away and the guard is easy to omit in new code.
findings.suggestion: Give each render an AbortController, accept a signal in api() (app/src/api.js:37), and abort on the next navigation — cancels the network work and removes the token checks.

findings.issue: No loading="lazy"/decoding="async" on card sprites; 48 sprites per home page and potentially several hundred cards on type/ability/move pages all download eagerly.
findings.suggestion: Add loading="lazy" decoding="async" to card sprites; keep the single Pokémon artwork image eager.

findings.issue: Pages are template literals with ~30 interpolation sites where forgetting escapeHtml/escapeAttr (app/src/api.js:88-98) injects API data as HTML; one missed escape is an XSS.
findings.suggestion: Introduce an auto-escaping tagged template `html` helper (~15 lines) so escaping is the default rather than per-call-site discipline.

findings.issue: Moves panel updates swap outerHTML then recursively re-attach handlers (439-441, 457-459); sort clicks also destroy the sort button, losing keyboard focus.
findings.suggestion: Delegate one click and one change listener on #moves and re-render only the table bodies; re-focus the sort button after render.

findings.issue: No types at the API boundary; PokeAPI resource shapes exist only implicitly in property chains with inconsistent optional chaining across app/src/main.js:596-720.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedef for Species/Pokemon/Type/Move and annotate api()'s return — zero tooling cost in plain-JS Vite.

findings.issue: Static assets served with no Cache-Control header although Vite emits content-hashed /assets filenames that never change between builds.
findings.suggestion: Send Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable for /assets/* and must-revalidate for index.html.

findings.issue: Runtime config injected by string-splicing a script before </head> and read from a window.__API_BASE_URL__ global (app/src/api.js:3); the splice silently degrades if the built HTML ever lacks </head>.
findings.suggestion: Serve a /runtime-config.js module the app imports, or at minimum assert the splice succeeded at startup.

findings.issue: Card sprites built from a hardcoded /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png pattern instead of API-provided sprite URLs, coupling the card grid to the media layout.
findings.suggestion: Keep the constructed URL as the documented fallback (the spec sanctions the pattern for the species list), but derive from pokemon.sprites.front_default wherever a Pokémon resource is already fetched, and comment the spec citation.

summary: A lean, current-generation vanilla+Vite app: one dependency (Vite 8.3.5, today's stable), zero build config, platform-first data access, and a clean two-module data layer that isolates all API access and configuration. Its forward-looking weaknesses are concentrated in the render layer: a History-API router where the now-Baseline Navigation API is the current choice, manual render-token cancellation instead of AbortController, no lazy image loading, and XSS safety resting on per-call-site escaping discipline rather than an enforced helper. I'd merge once the router, AbortController and escaping-helper items are addressed; none are architectural.

apis.replacement: Navigation API (navigation.addEventListener('navigate')), Baseline Newly available Jan 2026 — current-generation platform routing; History API remains supported, not deprecated
